Rashi on Gittin 46a:11:1.hebrew: אדם רוצה שתתבזה - כלומר, אינו מקפיד בכך; הלכך, צריך חקירת חכם — מצי לקלקלה:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:11:1.english: A man wants [her] to be disgraced - That is to say, he does not mind it; therefore, [in the case of a vow that] requires the inquiry of a sage, he can ruin her [by claiming the divorce was in error]:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:13:1.english: What did [the Tanna] teach - earlier [in the Mishnah? Did he teach] about vows that he [the husband] took?

Rashi on Gittin 46a:13:2.english: That he teaches [this] incident - Are we not dealing only with vows that she vowed?

Rashi on Gittin 46a:14:1.english: However, [if] he took a vow - [meaning] that he would divorce her:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:14:2.hebrew: יחזיר - אם ירצה, דליכא למיחש לקלקולא:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:14:2.english: He may remarry [her] - if he wishes, since there is no [need] to be concerned for ruin:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:1:1.hebrew: משום נדר אני מוציאך - בההוא אסרו רבנן להחזיר, ואי לא אמר, מותר להחזיר:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:1:1.english: Due to a vow I am sending you out - In that [case] the Rabbis forbade [him] to take [her] back, and if he did not say [this], he is permitted to take [her] back:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:1:3.hebrew: טעמא - דמתני' משום קלקולא, שלא יקלקלנה על בעלה לאחר שתנשא לאחר, ויאמר: "אילו הייתי יודע שהדברים בדאין או שהנדר יש לו הפרה, אפילו היו נותנין לי מאה מנה לא הייתי מגרשיך, וכן אמרתי בשעת גירושין שמפני כך אני מוציאך, וכשגרשתיך היה בדעתי להחזירך אם ימצאו דברים בדאים" — ונמצא גט בטל, ובניה מן השני ממזרין. לפיכך אומרים לו קודם גירושין: "הוי יודע שלא תחזירנה עולמית", ושוב אינו נאמן לומר כן, שכיון שידע שאסור לו להחזירה אפילו לא תנשא לאחר, ולא חש להמתין ולבדוק אחר הדברים, גילה בדעתו שלא היתה חביבה עליו:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:1:3.english: The reason - [of] the Mishnah is due to [potential] ruin, so that he will not ruin her [standing] with her husband after she marries another [man] and say: "Had I known that the matters were fabricated or that the vow had [grounds for] annulment, even if they had given me a hundred maneh I would not have divorced you; and indeed I said at the time of the divorce that for this [reason] I am sending you away, and when I divorced you I intended to take you back if the matters were found [to be] fabricated" — and thus the bill of divorce would be found void, and her children from the second [husband] would be mamzerim. Therefore, they say to him before the divorce: "Know that you may never take her back," and then he is no longer believed to say this, for since he knew that it is forbidden for him to take her back even [if] she does not marry another [man], and he did not care to wait and investigate the matters, he revealed his mind that she was not dear to him:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:1:4.hebrew: ואי לא לא מצי מקלקל לה - שהרי לא אמר שמוציאה משום שם רע, וכיון דלא מצי לקלקלה משניסת, לא אסרו לו להחזירה עד שלא ניסת:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:1:4.english: And if not, he cannot cause her harm - For he did not say that he is sending her out due to an ill repute, and since he cannot cause her harm once she has married [another man], [the Sages] did not forbid him from taking her back before she has married [another man]:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:2:1.hebrew: וצריך שיאמר כו' - תקנו חכמים למוציאה שיאמר לה כן, ומיהו בין אמר בין לא אמר, לא יחזיר:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:2:1.english: And he must say, etc. - The Sages instituted for one who divorces her that he should say this to her; however, whether he said [it] or did not say [it], he may not take [her] back:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:2:2.hebrew: קסבר טעמא - דלא יחזיר, משום קנס הוא, שלא יהו בנות ישראל כו':
Rashi on Gittin 46a:2:2.english: He holds [that] the reason - that he may not take [her] back is because of a penalty, so that Jewish women [will not be promiscuous], etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:4:1.hebrew: ונמצאו דברים בדאין - של שם רע, וה"ה לענין נדר דהותר:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:4:1.english: And the matters will be found [to be] fabricated - [those] of a bad reputation, and the same applies to the matter of a vow, that it was dissolved:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:4:2.hebrew: אומרים לו - קודם גירושין; וכיון דלא חש וגרשה, תו לא מצי לקלקלה, דגלי דעתיה דלא חביבה עליו כולי האי:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:4:2.english: One says to him - Before [the] divorce; and since he was not concerned [about this] and divorced her, he can no longer ruin her [by voiding the divorce], for he has revealed his mind that she is not all that dear to him:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:6:1.hebrew: מ"ט דרבי יהודה - דאמר נדר שהודר ברבים, אין לו הפרה:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:6:1.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda - who says [that] a vow that was vowed in public has no annulment:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:6:2.english: And they did not strike them - [This] is written regarding the Gibeonites:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:6:3.hebrew: נשבעו להם - והוה להו לאתשולי אשבועתייהו, אי לאו משום דהודר ברבים:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:6:3.english: Swore to them - and they could have requested absolution for their oath, were it not [for the fact] that it was vowed in public:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:7:1.english: And the Rabbis - who say that it can be dissolved:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:7:2.hebrew: התם - לאו משום דאין לו הפרה הוא, דאפילו הפרה לא צריך, דמי חיילה שבועה עלייהו כלל? הלא בטעות היתה:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:7:2.english: There - It is not because it has no annulment, for it does not even require annulment; for did the oath take effect upon them at all? Was it not [made] in error:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:7:3.hebrew: משום קדושת השם - שלא יאמרו העובדי כוכבים, "עברו על שבועתן":
Rashi on Gittin 46a:7:3.english: Due to the sanctity of [God's] Name - so that the idolaters would not say, "They violated their oath":

Rashi on Gittin 46a:9:1.hebrew: ימים שנים, רבים ג' - גבי זבה דרשינן הכי בשילהי נדה:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:9:1.english: "Days" [means] two, "many" [means] three - Regarding a zava, we expound [the verse] this way at the end of [Tractate] Niddah:

Rashi on Gittin 46a:9:2.hebrew: עדה - עשרה, דכתיב גבי מרגלים (במדבר י״ד:כ״ז): "לעדה הרעה", יצאו יהושע וכלב:
Rashi on Gittin 46a:9:2.english: Congregation - [A congregation consists of] ten, as it is written regarding the spies (Numbers 14:27): "[this] evil congregation" — Joshua and Caleb were excluded [leaving ten]:

Tosafot on Gittin 46a:1:1.hebrew: אי אמר לה הכי מצי מקלקל לה - נראה דחששא זו אינה כי אם לעז בעלמא, ולא שיהיה ממש גט בטל ובניה ממזרים, דהא לא אמר ע"מ; דאע"ג דבכמה דוכתי מהני גילוי דעת, כמו שטר מברחת דהאשה שנפלו (כתובות דף עט.), וזבין ולא איצטריכו ליה זוזי דפרק אלמנה ניזונת (כתובות דף צז.), הכא ליכא למימר הכי, מדבעי לר"מ תנאי כפול. לכך נראה דלא אתי אלא ללעז בעלמא, שיוציא עליה לעז כדי להחזירה, אע"ג דכבר נישאת לאחר, שריא ליה דזנות דשוגג הוא; לכך אמרו חכמים דלא יחזיר, דהשתא שוב לא יוציא לעז. ורש"י פי' דאפילו יאמר "אילו הייתי יודע" כו', אינו נאמן, דכיון דיודע שאסור להחזירה ולא חש להמתין ולבדוק אחר הדברים, גילה בדעתו שלא היתה חביבה עליו. ולר"מ דבעי תנאי כפול, כי לא כפליה למילתיה אפילו לעז ליכא; והא דקאמר ר"מ "כל נדר שצריך חקירת חכם לא יחזיר", היינו בדכפליה למילתיה ולא כפליה לתנאיה, דאי כפליה לתנאיה, אין מועיל מה שלא יחזיר, דלעולם איכא קלקולא:
Tosafot on Gittin 46a:1:1.english: If he said this to her, he is able to cause her harm - It appears that this concern is only [about] a mere rumor, and not that the bill of divorce would actually be void and her children [from a second marriage] mamzerim, for he did not say "on condition" [that the vow is valid]; for even though in several places a disclosure of intent is effective — such as [the case of] a deed of evasion in [the chapter entitled] HaIsha SheNaflu (Ketubot 79a), and [the case of one who] sold [property] and did not need the money in the chapter [entitled] Almana Nizonet (Ketubot 97a) — here one cannot say so, since according to Rabbi Meir a doubled condition is required. Therefore, it appears that [this concern] only addresses a mere rumor, that he might spread a rumor about her in order to take her back — [for] even though she has already married another [man], she is permitted to him [if the divorce was void], since [her relationship with the second husband] is unwitting adultery; therefore, the Sages said that he shall not remarry [her], so that now he will no longer spread a rumor. And Rashi explained that even if he says, "Had I known..." etc., he is not believed; for since he knows that it is forbidden to take her back and did not care to wait and investigate the matter, he revealed his intent that she was not dear to him. And according to Rabbi Meir, who requires a doubled condition, when he did not double his statement, there is not even a rumor; and that which Rabbi Meir says, "Any vow that requires the inquiry of a Sage, he shall not remarry [her]," refers to where he doubled his statement but did not double his condition — for if he doubled his condition, his not remarrying [her] would be of no avail, as there would always be [actual] harm:

Tosafot on Gittin 46a:2:1.hebrew: שלא יהו בנות ישראל פרוצות כו' - הני תרי לישני דרב יוסף אליבא דת"ק פליגי, דלישנא קמא סבר: כיון דקתני במתניתין נמי משום שם רע, והתם אין שייך פריצות — דמה לה לעשות אם מוציאין ש"ר עליה? — אלא טעמא משום קלקולא הוא. ולישנא בתרא סבר דבמוציא ש"ר לא מצי מקלקל לה, דכיון דמשום ש"ר מגרשה, דעתו בכל ענין לגרשה, אפי' יהא בטל; וכן בנדרים, דמסתברא דחד טעמא הוי בתרוייהו. והשתא אתי שפיר דמייתי "תניא כלישנא קמא" מדר"מ את"ק, דלא מייתי אלא דשייך במוציא ש"ר משום קלקולא, והוא הדין לת"ק. וא"ת: ללישנא בתרא דרב יוסף, דטעמא משום פריצותא, מנא לן דפליגי רבנן עליה דר' יהודה וסברי דנדר שהודר ברבים יש לו הפרה, דקאמר "ורבנן מי חיילא כו'"? וי"ל דהך סוגיא אתיא כלישנא קמא, דטעמייהו משום קלקול. א"נ, הא דקאמר "ורבנן", היינו ר"מ ור"א דאמרי "לא אסרו צריך כו'", דקסברי טעמא משום קלקולא, ואפילו בהודר ברבים קאמר דלא אסרו אלא מפני שאינו צריך; דאי ברבים אסור משום פריצותא, הו"ל למיסר "לא ידעו בו רבים" אטו מפני ד"ידעו בו רבים", ולא מפני ש"אין צריך":
Tosafot on Gittin 46a:2:1.english: So that Jewish women will not be promiscuous, etc. - These two versions of Rav Yosef [bar Minyumi] disagree according to the Tanna Kamma [of the Mishnah]. For the first version holds: since the Mishnah also teaches [the case of] "due to a bad reputation," and there [the concern of] promiscuity does not apply — for what can she do if people spread a bad reputation about her? — rather, the reason [for the prohibition] is because of [potential] harm [to her]. And the latter version holds that in [the case of] one who divorces [his wife] due to a bad reputation, he cannot cause harm to her [by invalidating the bill of divorce]; for since he is divorcing her due to a bad reputation, his intention is to divorce her in any event, even if [the rumor] should turn out to be baseless; and likewise with vows, for it is reasonable that there is one reason for both of them. And now it works out well that [the Gemara] brings [the baraita] "It was taught in accordance with the first version" from Rabbi Meir [to apply] to the Tanna Kamma; for [the baraita] only brings [a case] where [it] applies to one who divorces [his wife] due to a bad reputation because of [potential] harm, and the same law applies to the Tanna Kamma. And if you ask: According to the latter version of Rav Yosef, that the reason is because of promiscuity, from where do we know that the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yehuda and hold that a vow taken in public can be dissolved, as [the Gemara] says, "And the Rabbis [say]: Did it take effect, etc."? One can say that this sugya follows the first version, where their reason is because of [potential] harm. Alternatively, that which [the Gemara] says, "And the Rabbis," refers to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Elazar, who say, "They prohibited [a vow that] requires [dissolution] only [due to one that does not require dissolution]," for they hold the reason is because of [potential] harm; and even regarding [a vow] taken in public, [Rabbi Elazar] says that they only prohibited [remarriage] because of [a vow that] does not require [dissolution]. For if [a vow taken] in public were prohibited because of promiscuity, he should have [said that they] prohibited "[a vow that] the public was not aware of" on account of "[a vow that] the public was aware of," and not because of "[a vow that] does not require [dissolution]":

Tosafot on Gittin 46a:7:1.hebrew: כיון דאמרו מארץ רחוקה וכו' - וא"ת, בלא"ה מי חיילא שבועה, והא הוי נשבע לבטל את המצוה, דכתיב (דברים כ׳:ט״ז): "לא תחיה כל נשמה"! ואע"ג דאמרי' בירושלמי דשביעית פרק ששי: אמר רבי שמואל בר נחמני, שלש פרוזדוגמאות שלח יהושע לארץ ישראל עד שלא יכנסו לארץ: מי שהוא רוצה לפנות — יפנה, להשלים — ישלים, לעשות מלחמה — יעשה מלחמה; גרגשי פינה והלך לאפריקא, גבעונים השלימו, שנא' (יהושע י׳:א׳): "וכי השלימו יושבי גבעון את ישראל", שלשים ואחד מלכים עשו מלחמה ונפלו — היינו קודם שעברו את הירדן, כדקאמר "עד שלא יכנסו לארץ"; אבל משנכנסו, משמע שלא היו יכולין להשלים, ולכך הוצרכו להערים ולומר "מארץ רחוקה באנו"? וי"ל, דעל כרחך באין רוצים להשלים כתיב "לא תחיה כל נשמה", כדמוכחי קראי (דברים כ׳:י׳-י״א): "וקראת אליה לשלום וגו' ואם לא תשלים עמך וגו' רק מערי העמים וגו' לא תחיה כל נשמה". וא"ת, מ"ט דרבי יהודה, הא ודאי שבועה בטעות הואי? ועוד, לר' יהודה איך הניחום בארץ, הכתיב (שמות כ״ג:ל״ג): "לא ישבו בארצך וגו'", והוה ליה נשבע לבטל את המצוה, וע"כ משום חילול השם הוא כדאמרי רבנן! וי"ל, דקסבר ר' יהודה דאי איתא דיש לו הפרה, לא היה בדבר חילול השם. וא"ת, בלא חילול השם נמי אין יכולין להורגן כיון דבאין להתגייר, כדאמרינן לעיל (גיטין דף מה.): "לא ישבו בארצך פן יחטיאו אותך לי — יכול בעובד כוכבים שקיבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים כו'"; ואמרינן נמי בפרק אלו נאמרין (סוטה דף לה:): "וכתבו להן מלמטה 'למען אשר לא ילמדו אתכם לעשות וגו'' — הא למדת שאם חוזרין בתשובה שמקבלין אותן", וההוא קרא בז' אומות כתיב? וי"ל, דאי לאו חילול השם, נהי שלא היו יכולין להרגן, היו יכולין לגרשן מעריהם; ועוד, דבאותה שעה לא באו להתגייר, כי אם אחרי כן:
Tosafot on Gittin 46a:7:1.english: Since they said, “From a far country,” etc. - And if you ask: Even without this, did the oath take effect? Behold, it is [a case of] one who swears to nullify a mitzva, as it is written (Deuteronomy 20:16): “You shall not leave any soul alive”! And even though we say in the Jerusalem Talmud, [Tractate] Shevi'it, chapter six: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: Joshua sent three proclamations to the Land of Israel before they entered the Land: Whoever wishes to depart — let him depart; [whoever wishes] to make peace — let him make peace; [whoever wishes] to wage war — let him wage war. The Girgashite departed and went to Africa; the Gibeonites made peace, as it is stated (Joshua 10:1): “And how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel”; thirty-one kings waged war and fell — that was before they crossed the Jordan, as it says, “before they entered the Land”; but once they entered, it is implied that they could no longer make peace, and therefore they needed to act cunningly and say, “We have come from a far country”? And one can say: Perforce, [the verse] “You shall not leave any soul alive” is written regarding those who do not wish to make peace, as the verses prove (Deuteronomy 20:10–11): “And you shall proclaim peace to it, etc., and if it does not make peace with you, etc., only from the cities of the peoples, etc., you shall not leave any soul alive.” And if you ask: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda — behold, this was certainly an oath [made] in error? And furthermore, according to Rabbi Yehuda, how did they leave them in the Land? Is it not written (Exodus 23:33): “They shall not dwell in your land, etc.,” so it is [a case of] one who swears to nullify a mitzva, and perforce it is because of [preventing] the desecration of God’s name, as the Rabbis say! And one can say: Rabbi Yehuda holds that if it were true that it [could be] dissolved, there would be no desecration of God’s name in the matter. And if you ask: Even without [the concern of] desecration of God’s name, they could not kill them since they came to convert, as we say above (Gittin 45a): “‘They shall not dwell in your land lest they cause you to sin against Me’ — might [this apply even] to an idolater who accepted upon himself not to worship idols, etc.”; and we also say in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Ne'emarin (Sotah 35b): “And they wrote below them: ‘So that they do not teach you to do, etc.’ — from here you learn that if they repent, we accept them,” and that verse is written regarding the seven nations? And one can say: Were it not for [the concern of] desecration of God’s name, granted that they could not kill them, they could have expelled them from their cities; and furthermore, at that time they did not come to convert, only afterward:

Tosafot on Gittin 46a:8:1.hebrew: רב נחמן בר יצחק אמר שלשה - נראה דעל דעת רבים לא בעי אלא שנים, דבפרק שבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף לט.) כשאמר להם משה לישראל: הוו יודעים שלא על דעתכם אני משביע אתכם וכו', ופירש שם בקונטרס דהיינו על דעת רבים. ומיהו, לפ"ז לא היה היתר לחרמות בזמן הזה. ונראה דלא אמר משה כן אלא שלא יערימו, כדמפרש התם משום קניא דרבא; וכן עתה אין עושין אלא בשביל כך. וא"ת: על דעת יחיד נמי לא יהא לו הפרה, כיון דתלה בו נדרו. וי"ל: דמבטל דעתו משום רבים, ולא משום יחיד:
Tosafot on Gittin 46a:8:1.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says: Three - It appears that [a vow made] on the authority of the public requires only two [people], for in the chapter [entitled] Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shevuot 39a), when Moses said to Israel: "Know that not according to your mind do I adjure you, etc.," [Rashi] explained there in the Kuntres that this is [an oath] on the authority of the public. However, according to this, there would be no annulment for bans nowadays. Rather, it appears that Moses only said this so that they would not act with subterfuge, as [the Gemara] explains there because of [the incident of] Rava's reed; and so too nowadays, they only do [so] for that reason. And if you ask: [A vow made] on the authority of an individual should also have no annulment, since he made his vow dependent upon him! One can answer that he nullifies his [own] intent on account of the public, and not on account of an individual:
